text:
kai: FYI starting Tide11B onboarding (gguf -> hf). quick smoke showed reranker MRR drop when running int8-grouped quant (gsize=64) vs fp16. short examples attached.

anya: can you paste conversion+quant commands?

kai: sure:
```n# convert and quant
python3 tools/convert_gguf.py --input tide11b.gguf --out tide11b.hf --format hf --rotary-scale 1.0
python3 tools/quantize.py --in tide11b.hf --out tide11b.int8 --mode grouped --group-size 64 --perchannel --dtype int8
```

mohit: interesting that it's int8 grouped. is the tokenizer unchanged? we had token-normalizer changes that flip NFKC in some pipelines.

kai: I compared tokenizer vocabs: token_count identical, checksums of bpe merges match, but end-of-sequence id differs (upstream 2 vs our conversion 3) because of an anchor-reserve step in convert script. i assumed harmless but maybe not.

anya: does fp16 baseline use the same converted hf weights?

kai: yes fp16 vs upstream match on our long rerank eval (MRR ~0.762). int8 grouped drops to 0.711 on same eval.

bench-bot: Tide11B | eval/rerank_longlist | fp16: MRR 0.762 | int8_group64: MRR 0.711 | int8_nongroup: MRR 0.759

mohit: aha non-grouped int8 is fine. suggests grouping packer bug. maybe head-permute or projection order changed when we flatten groups for quant.

anya: could also be per-head scale mismatch: grouped int8 uses a shared scale across group of 64 elements, if we accidentally align groups across head boundaries we can mix head scales. check first attention projection weight shapes and scale offsets used by quant metadata.

kai: grabbed quant metadata: group_scale_offsets start at [0, 64, 128, ...] as expected. but when loading into runtime packed kernel we saw reorder map that permuted dims by 2 for optimization.

mohit: do we have a repro that shows top-k rerank flip? small reproducer would help narrow it to attention vs embeddings.

kai: made a tiny repro that scores 5 candidates. With fp16 top1 is docA, int8_group64 top1 becomes docD. Logging attention scores per-candidate shows sharp drop on cross-attention logits in layer 10.

anya: layer 10 cross-attn drift points to projection packing. can you dump per-head q/k/v norms before/after quant load for layer10?

kai: did that: fp16 q_norms head0..7: [1.12,1.09,1.11,1.10,1.08,1.07,1.09,1.10]
int8_group64 q_norms: [1.12,1.09,0.62,1.10,1.08,1.07,1.09,1.10]

mohit: head2 is half scale. that screams group boundary split across head axis when applying scale. maybe the packer computes group index using linear offset without considering head stride. if group_size matches head_width * 2 or similar it can slice differently.

anya: also double-check rotary frequency application: if q/k indices shift into the wrong position due to grouping reorder, rotary phase for those heads will be off causing cross-attn mismatch for longer contexts. but your repro is shortlist (512 tokens) so still maybe just quant scale.

kai: confirmed: disabling grouped quant (use per-tensor int8) fixes MRR. switching to group-size=32 also fixes it. so boundary at 64 triggers bug.

bench-bot: Issue filed: #4876  quant_packer: group-boundary misaligns across head axis at group_size multiple of head_width*? (repro + traces attached)

mohit: likely root cause in quant_packer.c: group_idx = (flat_offset / group_size); but later when reshaping to [heads, head_dim] they use integer division again without recomputing base offset -> double-offset. I'll push a minimal PR to correct indexing math and add test.

anya: for immediate mitigation let's blacklist Tide11B grouped-int8 gsize=64 in model registry and mark onboard status as "int8-group64-unavailable". also run int8_group64 smoke across new models where head_dim divides 64.

kai: done: added blacklist entry to model_metadata.yaml and uploaded int8_nongroup artifact to gs://redwood-models/tide11b/177999/

bench-bot: Tide11B | eval/rerank_longlist | int8_nongroup: MRR 0.759 (passes)

mohit: PR incoming with fix + unit test reproducing head-scale mismatch. please include attention-norm diff check in our quant-validation harness.

anya: long-term: add CI matrix entry to test group_size values that are multiples/divisors of typical head widths (32,64,128) for all new model onboards. also add a small extraction that asserts q_norms per-head within tol after quant load.

kai: thanks all. leaving traces and mini-repro in #4876. tagging infra to run a cross-model scan next week. :wave:
